text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government dissatisfied with parliamentarians' remarks about the attempted assassination of leading opposition parliamentarian Abdullah al-Naibari on Friday. MPs, who suggested a link between the attempt and Naibari's efforts against alleged corruption, have lashed out at the government for what they said was lack of action against alleged abusers of public funds.
- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan denies resignation rumours.

- United Nations approves budget for the United Nations Iraq-Kuwait Observation Mission (UNIKOM) for 1998. Kuwait will shoulder two thirds of UNIKOM's budget. UNIKOM was created after the 1991 Gulf War to monitor the border between Kuwait and its former occupier Iraq.
- Islamic banking units manage 35 percent of Kuwait savings, Islamic investment firm official says.
- Cabinet reviews report on workers rights.
- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah meets today (Monday) with chief editors of the local press to discuss the latest local and regional developments.

- Parliament speaker Ahmad al-Saadoun officially asked the government to take out a projected revenue of about 200 million dinars from the 1997/98 proposed state budget. A parliamentary panel has suspended the budget that included income from rises in charges on state services, so far opposed by the house.
